facts.label: Financial interpretation

tables.title: Contrary evidence and what would change the view

rows.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 1
Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 2
Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- High: Issuer-adjusted EBITDA rests on fourteen add-backs for fiscal 2026 that the issuer does not classify as cash or non-cash, recurring or realised, and the Credit Agreement measure adds an annualisation of Kito Crosby, the divestiture and expected synergies that cannot be reproduced. The adjusted ratios are therefore usable as the issuer's view only; component support from the issuer and the credit agreement definitions would close this. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14 - High: Covenant headroom is not established: the credit agreement's first lien leverage ceiling of 7.75x is not matched by a reported first lien ratio, and the waiver of the AR securitization facility's delinquency and default ratios at 2026-09-30 and its amendment on 2026-10-29 are described but not supplied. The test levels, definitions and any cure terms would be needed to size headroom. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59 - Medium: The acquired business's own statements and pre-acquisition earnings are not supplied, so the twelve-month figures hold Kito Crosby only from 2026-02-03 and no full-year pro forma EBITDA other than the issuer's annualised figure can be built. This understates the earnings base and overstates reported leverage until twelve months of actual results exist. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 14 - Medium: Legal ranking, lien priority and guarantor scope across the term loan, notes, revolver and AR facility are not stated in the documents read, so the debt stack chart has no ranked rows and no secured or senior subtotal is formed. The credit agreement, indenture and guarantee schedules would close this. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 111; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27 - Medium: The annual report prints the revolver maturity as 2028-02-03 in one paragraph and as 2031-02-03 in the next, and the September 2026 report states 2031-02-03. The later date is used; the earlier one may carry over from the previous facility. The credit agreement would settle it. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 111–112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29; 10-Q_2025-12-31_cmco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25 - Medium: The market risk section of the annual report states there are no pay-fixed swaps while the derivatives note describes eleven with a notional of USD 965 million, so the hedged share of the floating-rate debt is not established. Interest sensitivity to rates therefore cannot be sized. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26 - Medium: Free cash flow and operating cash flow include deal, integration and refinancing cash costs that the documents do not separate, so underlying cash generation and the run rate after integration are not established. A cash flow bridge from the issuer would close this. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55 - Low: The annual report's own date is recorded by its signature page as 2026-06-08 while two later quarterly reports say it was filed on 2026-06-02. This changes no figure but the filing date remains unresolved; the filing record would settle it. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 164; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8 - Low: The June 2026 release prints closing cash of 97,234 for fiscal 2026 against 97,023 in the annual report and in its own roll-forward; the annual report figure is used and the difference is 0.211 US$m. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 78 - Low: Issuer-adjusted EBITDA for the first half of fiscal 2027 differs by 0.021 US$m from the two quarters because the six-month stock-based compensation add-back differs; the six-month figure is used. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-07-30_exhibit99107302026.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13 - Low: No release states issuer-adjusted EBITDA for fiscal 2024, the third quarter of fiscal 2026 or the nine months to 2025-12-31, so those cells are not supplied; depreciation and amortization for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 is calculated because no document prints it. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2025-12-31_cmco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7 - Low: Source dashes are carried as not supplied rather than zero, including the fiscal 2025 sale-of-business proceeds and the preferred stock and noncontrolling interest lines at March 2025; the noncontrolling interest and equity attributable lines are not printed in the December 2025 report. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2025-12-31_cmco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5 - Low: The company reports one segment, so no segment revenue schedule is built, and capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth; backlog and receivable statistics after March 2026 are not stated in the later releases, and the issuer states no funds-from-operations measure, so none is built. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 149; EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 3 - Low: Small uncommitted non-U.S. bank lines of USD 5.438 million, of which USD 0.566 million was drawn, and USD 18.757 million of bank guarantees in use are not part of the debt instrument table or total debt, and where the drawn amount is classified is not stated; the amounts are immaterial to leverage but would be debt-like if drawn. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31 - Low: Pension and operating lease balances are taken at March 2026 only and their September 2026 values are not extracted, and the terms of the preferred dividend between cash and payment in kind are stated but the election for the current year is not. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 109; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 149; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33 - Low: The issuer's Credit Agreement net debt deducts AR securitization obligations of 42.762 while the September 2026 report prints 42.588, and the earnings bases differ, so the issuer's 4.9x cannot be reconciled to carrying net debt line by line. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30

facts.text: A material part of the earnings behind the leverage measure is annualised, not yet earned. That add-back was 59.94% of the measure at March 2026, when it included USD 70.64 million of expected synergies. Creditors should read the 4.9x ratio as management-normalised, not measured. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The capital structure is debt-heavy with a growing senior equity layer rather than common equity beneath the debt. New secured debt of USD 2,550.00 million and USD 800.00 million of 7% preferred raised USD 538.09 million more than the purchase price, a sum the filings do not break down between refinancing, fees and cash. The preferred accreted USD 37.43 million through September 2026 and the issuer guides to paying it in kind during FY2027; paid in cash it would cost about USD 58.62 million a year on a simple calculation, against USD 4.04 million of common dividends in H1 FY2027. Debt holders gain from the cash retained, but the preferred claim grows ahead of common holders and would compete for cash if the election changed. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: CD&R holds influence and a senior claim, but the documents read show no extraction, so governance risk is medium rather than high or low. The investor owns all of the Series A preferred, may name up to three directors, has preemptive rights to keep its pro rata stake and would hold about 43.45% as converted at September 2026 on a calculation that ignores unvested awards, up from 42.48% at issue because the dividend accretes. The annual report itself warns that the investor's interests may differ from other holders. No fees, related-party dealings or creditor-adverse transactions appear in the filings read, but the agreements that would show consent rights and fees were not supplied, so capacity and willingness cannot be separated. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The operating franchise is defensive in its consumables and installed base, yet sales are cyclical, distributor-led and exposed to steel and component costs. Management describes the safety-critical products as frequently replaced, most distributors have no written agreement with the issuer, and raw materials were 51% of cost of products sold in FY2026 against 59% a year earlier, a fall that overstates any improvement because the numerator excludes Kito Crosby while the denominator includes it. Hoists are 46.68% of sales, the precision conveying line shrank 3.94% and carries a USD 200.00 million goodwill impairment, and legacy growth is modest: Legacy CMCO net sales grew 5.3% in Q2 FY2027, while total backlog rose 61.12% by March 2026 mainly because Kito Crosby brought USD 199.89 million of it. facts.text: Disclosure supports monitoring, but several items are inconsistent, undated or unexplained, and each caps confidence. The purchase price is printed as USD 2,700.00 million, USD 2,811.91 million and USD 2,821.91 million at announcement, closing and after a final adjustment paid after quarter end. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is trading momentum and cash retention. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 20.6% in Q2 FY2027 against 15.4% a year earlier, orders rose 122% largely through the acquisition, and the issuer raised its FY2027 net sales and Adjusted EBITDA guidance twice, to USD 2,130 million to USD 2,170 million and USD 425 million to USD 440 million. Liquidity of USD 531.98 million is far above the USD 17.98 million of principal due in FY2027 and the USD 69.90 million due in FY2029, the sponsor's USD 800.00 million is equity behind the debt and is being paid in kind, and the 50 bp margin cut lowers interest cost. If these hold, the medium governance rating and the doubts about the annualised leverage measure would both ease. facts.text: Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. Further analysis requires the investment agreement, the proxy statement and the AR facility waiver terms.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage is high, and the lower figure the issuer reports depends on annualised earnings. Net debt of USD 2,301.41 million at 2026-09-30, or USD 2,303.44 million pro forma for the common dividend payable on 2026-11-16, is 6.95x issuer-adjusted twelve-month EBITDA of USD 331.19 million, and 6.95x pro forma. The issuer's 4.9x uses USD 467.80 million of earnings that add USD 132.39 million of annualised acquisition earnings and expected synergies, and reported EBITDA of USD 10.03 million is too small to give a ratio. The twelve-month window holds Kito Crosby only from 2026-02-03, so the ratio falls as acquired earnings enter even if net debt does not, and creditors should underwrite a path down from 6.95x rather than the 4.9x already shown. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 14; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation N01

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Cash generation does not yet support deleveraging. Free cash flow was USD 4.60 million in H1 FY2027 after a negative USD 15.36 million in Q2 FY2027, which is 2.07% of H1 Adjusted EBITDA, and negative USD 153.19 million over the twelve months to September 2026 after deal and integration payments. Adjusted EBITDA covered interest and debt expense 2.31x in Q2 FY2027, and the issuer plans about USD 150.00 million of repayments in the next twelve months, of which H1 free cash flow covered only 3.07%. The plan therefore rests on a stronger H2, working capital release or revolver and cash use, not on cash flow already earned. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation N02; calculation N03; calculation N04

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for a better view is earnings momentum and delivery against guidance. Adjusted EBITDA margin rose 520 bp to 20.6% in Q2 FY2027, Legacy CMCO net sales grew 5.3%, synergies are described as ahead of plan, and guidance for Adjusted EBITDA was raised twice, to USD 425 million to USD 440 million. That guidance needs H2 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 202.35 million to USD 217.35 million against USD 222.65 million in H1 FY2027, so it does not require improvement, and the 50 bp term loan margin cut saves about USD 7.25 million a year. If H2 delivers and net debt starts to fall, leverage on the issuer's own basis would approach the reported 4.9x with real earnings behind it. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation N07; calculation N12

facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Columbus McKinnon designs, makes and markets lifting, rigging, conveying and motion-control products and, since 2026-02-03, includes Kito Crosby, a lifting and securement business that supplied 56.50% of H1 FY2027 net sales. The issuer describes its consumables as safety-critical and frequently replaced, which is management language but points to repeat demand tied to inspection cycles, while hoists, cranes and conveyors depend on industrial capital spending. Sales go mainly through distributors and crane builders, 44% of FY2026 sales were outside the United States, and there is one reporting segment. For creditors the replacement element supports cash-flow visibility and debt service, the cyclical element limits it, and the larger scale after the acquisition helps access to capital markets without removing the integration risk. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation N11

facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: CD&R XII Keystone Holdings, L.P. holds all of the Series A preferred, about 43% of the equity as converted, may name up to three directors and has preemptive rights, while the common shares are listed and the common holders are not named in the documents supplied. The parent borrows under the 2026 credit agreement and issued the notes, unnamed subsidiaries guarantee the notes, and the AR facility is borrowed through a financing subsidiary with the parent as performance guarantor. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is partly recurring and partly cyclical. In FY2026 price added USD 21.54 million and volume USD 10.15 million to net sales, and in Q2 FY2027 price added USD 10.06 million against USD 2.34 million from volume, so price supplied 81.14% of the organic gain in the quarter. That points to pricing power, but it also means volume growth is thin, and the issuer ties demand to industrial capacity utilisation, production indices, tariffs and interest rates. Backlog rose 61.12% to USD 519.64 million by March 2026 mainly through Kito Crosby, long-term backlog was 50.8% of the total, and book-to-bill was 1.0x in Q2 FY2027. Sales rest on distributors that choose what to stock and have no written agreements, and no customer or distributor concentration is stated. Revenue is therefore likely more predictable in its consumable and installed-base share, on management's description, and cyclical and discretionary in its project share, and not shown to be concentrated or structurally declining apart from the 3.94% fall in precision conveying. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Costs are weighted to materials and the pass-through is lagged. Raw materials and components were 51% of cost of products sold in FY2026, bought from a limited set of preferred suppliers on company-wide terms, and the issuer reports higher steel and component costs and tariffs. In FY2026 material inflation, tariffs and other cost changes net of price took USD 5.88 million from gross profit, unfavourable mix took USD 7.91 million and the divested business took USD 6.69 million, and the gross margin fell to 30.1% from 33.8% with USD 36.80 million of inventory step-up in cost of sales. In Q2 FY2027 the gross margin was 34.8% against 34.5% and the Adjusted gross margin 36.5% against 35.3%. The split between fixed and variable cost is not stated, so operating leverage cannot be measured; the evidence supports defending margins against input costs with price, with synergy savings as extra cushion, and does not show how margins behave under a volume fall. facts.label: Capital intensity and FCF conversion
facts.text: Capital needs are light and conversion of EBITDA to cash is weak for now. Capital expenditure was 1.50% of FY2026 net sales and USD 16.46 million in H1 FY2027, with USD 45 million to USD 55 million guided for FY2027, so capex is a lever of some size. Free cash flow was 2.07% of H1 FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA because interest, integration costs of USD 24.30 million year to date, cash taxes and an USD 55.04 million working capital outflow absorbed it, and net cash paid for income taxes was USD 45.85 million in FY2026 despite a net loss. Operating lease payments of USD 23.84 million fall due in FY2027. Deal-related payments depressed FY2026 and the first half, so conversion should improve as they end, but the guidance arithmetic leaves only USD 180.00 million to USD 210.00 million before taxes, integration and working capital, which is the amount that would fund the planned paydown. facts.label: Porter's five forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is the force that matters most for margins: the industry is fragmented, rivals include larger groups and some have greater financial resources and less debt, and competition on price could cut margin. Buyer power sits with distributors that decide what to stock and have no written agreements with the issuer, which limits pricing if they favour a rival. Supplier power is moderate: materials are available from several sources but the issuer buys from a limited set of preferred suppliers, and supply constraints have raised cost and lead times. The threat of new entrants and of substitutes is not established in the documents supplied, so no credit conclusion is drawn on either. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 57

facts.label: PEST analysis
facts.text: Two categories change credit capacity. Political and regulatory factors: tariffs raised input costs, and regulatory approval of the acquisition required the sale of the U.S. power chain hoist and chain business, which contributed USD 123.05 million of FY2026 sales and none after 2026-03-04. Economic factors: demand follows industrial capacity utilisation and production, 62.87% of debt floats, and 44% of sales are outside the United States, where a 10% move in the dollar changes income from operations by about USD 7.26 million. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials. facts.label: SWOT analysis
facts.text: Strengths are the replacement-driven consumable base, a broad distributor and service network, liquidity of USD 531.98 million with no large maturity before 2031, and sponsor equity of USD 800.00 million. Weaknesses are leverage that is high on actual earnings, thin free cash flow, goodwill and intangibles of 60.30% of total assets, concentration in hoists and in the United States, and cost exposure to steel and tariffs. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are synergy delivery and margin expansion, the 50 bp margin cut, and paydown from a recovering free cash flow. Threats that could weaken it are an industrial downturn with distributor destocking, a cash election on the preferred, a second waiver on the AR facility, and refinancing the USD 2,349.23 million of term loan and notes due in 2033 at higher leverage. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 110–111; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation N05; calculation N14

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strength one is liquidity and maturity profile. Cash and revolver availability of USD 531.98 million cover scheduled principal through FY2030 4.40 times, which lowers near-term refinancing and liquidity risk. Strength two is margin and synergy momentum: the Adjusted EBITDA margin rose 520 bp to 20.6% and guidance was raised twice, which would lower leverage if delivered. Strength three is sponsor equity: USD 800.00 million of preferred reduced the debt needed and is paid in kind, preserving cash. Strength four is a replacement-driven franchise whose safety-critical products support repeat demand, with no customer concentration disclosed. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months the issuer guides to FY2027 net sales of USD 2,130 million to USD 2,170 million, Adjusted EBITDA of USD 425 million to USD 440 million and interest expense of USD 185 million to USD 190 million. The guidance is 5.65% above pro forma FY2026 sales at its midpoint and needs H2 Adjusted EBITDA no higher than H1, which supports it, while guided Adjusted EBITDA covers guided interest 2.24x to 2.38x, so deleveraging depends on cash conversion and the planned paydown, not on cover. Company tailwinds are synergy delivery, the margin cut and lower deal costs; company headwinds are interest cost, integration spend and a cash election on the preferred. Sector tailwinds named by the issuer are automation and labour productivity trends and growth in Asia and other emerging markets; sector headwinds are tariffs, steel and component costs and a slowdown in industrial production. Over three to five years the 2029 call date of the notes, the 2031 revolver and the 2033 term loan and notes make deleveraging before 2033 the central task. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is an industrial slowdown with steel and tariff cost pressure that leads distributors, who hold the stocking decision and have no written agreements, to cut orders. The first operational break is a fall in short-cycle orders, with book-to-bill below 1.0x, followed by price giving way to volume and gross margin falling back from the 34.1% Adjusted gross margin of FY2026. Financially, on illustrative arithmetic that returns the Adjusted EBITDA margin to the 15.20% of FY2026 on the guided sales midpoint of USD 2,150 million, Adjusted EBITDA would be USD 326.80 million, interest cover 1.74x, and EBITDA less guided interest and capex USD 89.30 million before taxes, integration and working capital. Cash taxes at the FY2026 level of USD 45.85 million would leave USD 43.45 million, so the planned USD 150.00 million paydown would not be met from cash flow and the revolver would fund the gap. Revolver borrowings could rise by USD 90.36 million, or USD 71.08 million if letters of credit count, before the 30% level at which the first lien leverage covenant is tested, and the ratio against its 7.75x ceiling is not reported. Management levers are capex, which can be cut, the in-kind preferred dividend, a common dividend of USD 8.04 million a year, working capital release from USD 567.55 million of inventory and synergy savings. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis within 12 to 24 months because no principal above USD 69.90 million falls due before 2031, but it is not sufficient to protect the deleveraging plan, and the observable triggers are book-to-bill, the Adjusted EBITDA margin, revolver use, and any new AR facility waiver. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Columbus McKinnon presents an adequate business profile supported by replacement-driven products, a wide channel and added scale, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 6.95x on issuer-adjusted EBITDA (6.95x pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-11-16), thin free cash flow and integration risk. Cash-flow durability appears weak today and not yet demonstrated, because free cash flow was 2.07% of H1 Adjusted EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on cutting leverage before the 2033 term loan and notes come due, on extending the AR facility due 2028-08-11 and on keeping the revolver unused near the 30% covenant level. The primary downside path is a margin reversal on fixed interest charges that forces revolver use and defers deleveraging. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and first lien ratio, the investor agreements, Kito Crosby's standalone earnings, a rating and market prices. Top risk: leverage that depends on annualised earnings and unproven free cash flow. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation N01; calculation N03; calculation N10

## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied filings support credit work on Columbus McKinnon through the September 2026 quarter, but covenant, structural and market work cannot rest on them because no executed debt documents, ratings or market prices were supplied.

For creditors, the audited March 2026 statements and the two later quarterly reports give a usable view of the post-acquisition balance sheet and liquidity, yet any trend crossing the February 2026 acquisition of Kito Crosby compares two different perimeters. Covenant tests, guarantor coverage and board rights are known only from the issuer's own summaries, and the revolver maturity is stated two ways in the annual report. These are limits on the evidence, not findings about credit quality.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net debt is 6.95x issuer-adjusted EBITDA for the twelve months to September 2026, above the 4.9x the issuer reports on an annualised basis, so creditors should not rely on the lower figure until Kito Crosby has been owned for a full year. Net debt of USD 2,301.41 million (and USD 2,303.44 million after the dividend payable on 2026-11-16) has not fallen since March 2026, and reported EBITDA of USD 10.03 million over the same twelve months, after a USD 200 million goodwill impairment and deal costs, is too small to give a meaningful ratio.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C03; calculation C06; calculation C13; calculation C15

Liquidity of USD 531.98 million and no large maturity before fiscal 2029 give time, but adjusted cash interest cover is 2.75x and the AR securitization lender had to waive its delinquency tests at September 2026.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 115; calculation C08; calculation C09
### Key findings

The apparent fall in leverage is a denominator effect, not repayment. Net debt was USD 2,296.45 million in March 2026, USD 2,278.37 million in June and USD 2,301.41 million in September, so net debt over issuer-adjusted EBITDA moved from 12.66x to 8.76x and 6.95x only because Kito Crosby's earnings entered the twelve-month figure. The issuer's own 4.9x Credit Agreement ratio is lower again because its earnings add USD 132.39 million of annualised acquisition earnings and expected synergies, and its net debt excludes the AR securitization facility.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C03; calculation C06; calculation C15

Reported earnings are not a usable base. EBITDA before issuer adjustments was negative at USD 68.42 million for fiscal 2026 because the goodwill impairment, deal costs, inventory step-up and refinancing costs run through it. Issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 331.19 million for the twelve months to September 2026 therefore rests on add-backs the issuer defines: fourteen items added a net USD 249.8 million in fiscal 2026, led by the USD 200 million impairment, with a USD 103.31 million gain on a business sale deducted.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C05; calculation C12; calculation C21

Cash generation does not yet support the debt. Operating cash flow was negative at USD 125.39 million and free cash flow negative at USD 153.19 million over the twelve months to September 2026, dominated by fiscal 2026 when deal and integration costs were paid; in the first half of fiscal 2027 operating cash flow was USD 21.07 million and free cash flow USD 4.6 million. Capital expenditure is light at 1.57% of net sales, so deleveraging depends on operating cash flow recovering as integration costs fade.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C06; calculation C07

Interest cover is thin and the trailing figure flatters it. Issuer-adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.75x over the twelve months to September 2026, but that period holds only part of a year of interest on the new debt. Interest and debt expense in the September quarter was USD 48.05 million against quarterly issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 111.21 million, a cover of 2.31x, before any benefit from the 50 bp term loan margin cut that began on 2026-09-21.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C06; calculation C17

Liquidity is adequate for now but fell in the quarter. Cash of USD 110.9 million and revolver availability of USD 421.08 million make USD 531.98 million, down USD 35.17 million since June as revolver borrowings rose from USD 12.84 million to USD 59.64 million. The annual report's schedule shows only USD 17.98 million due in fiscal 2027 and USD 16.5 million in fiscal 2028 before USD 69.9 million in fiscal 2029 and USD 2,320.12 million after fiscal 2030, and the issuer plans to repay about USD 150 million in the next twelve months, already classed as current.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C19

The covenant package gives little comfort that can be measured. The key financial covenant is a first lien leverage ceiling of 7.75x that steps down to 6.25x and is tested only when revolver borrowings exceed 30% of commitments, a trigger that USD 59.64 million drawn against USD 500 million, or 11.93%, does not reach. The first lien ratio itself is not reported, so headroom is not established. The AR securitization lender waived its delinquency and default ratios at 2026-09-30 and the facility was amended again on 2026-10-29, and the documents do not say why.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C19; calculation C20

Claims outside total debt add to the burden. The USD 800 million of 7% convertible preferred shares sold to the sponsor are carried in equity at USD 818.4 million, including payment-in-kind dividends, and would convert into about 43% of the equity; operating lease liabilities were USD 95.72 million and the pension plans were underfunded by USD 78.25 million at March 2026, general and product liability reserves were USD 31.87 million before USD 19.74 million of expected insurance recoveries at September 2026, and USD 20 million is payable to the former owner of Kito Crosby.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is operating momentum and liquidity. The issuer-adjusted EBITDA margin was 20.8% in the first half of fiscal 2027 against 14.7% a year earlier, backlog at March 2026 was USD 519.6 million against USD 322.5 million a year before, and the issuer's annualised measure is 4.9x with cost synergies still to come. Liquidity is also well above scheduled maturities, and the key financial covenant is untested at current revolver use.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C15; calculation C19

The view would improve if actual twelve-month issuer-adjusted EBITDA, once Kito Crosby is in for a full year, brings net leverage clearly below the current figure while net debt falls, if free cash flow turns positive after integration costs and cash interest, and if the AR securitization facility passes its tests without waivers. It would worsen if revolver borrowings keep rising toward the 30% trigger, if the waiver is repeated, or if quarterly adjusted EBITDA stops covering interest and debt expense by a wide margin.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C17; calculation C19

### Financial interpretation

Leverage trajectory and drivers. Debt rose from USD 470.98 million in March 2025 to USD 2,393.01 million in March 2026 because Kito Crosby was bought with a new term loan, USD 900 million of senior secured notes due 2033 and USD 800 million of preferred equity, and then rose a further USD 19.3 million to USD 2,412.31 million by September 2026. Net debt over reported EBITDA is 229.41x in September and not meaningful in March and June because reported EBITDA is negative; the issuer-adjusted ratios of 12.66x, 8.76x and 6.95x fall only as acquired earnings are added to the twelve-month window.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 109; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C11

Coverage. Reported EBITDA does not cover cash interest in any period since March 2026, and issuer-adjusted cover is 3.97x for fiscal 2026 on a full year of the old capital structure and only about two months of the new one, 3.88x to June and 2.75x to September. The quarterly view, 2.31x on interest and debt expense, is the better indicator of the current burden. No funds-from-operations measure is stated by the issuer and none is built here.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C06; calculation C17

Cash-flow quality. Free cash flow was negative at USD 164.07 million in fiscal 2026, when working capital absorbed cash through the payment of Kito Crosby deal and success fees, and USD 4.6 million in the first half of fiscal 2027. Capital expenditure of 1.57% of net sales leaves little discretionary spending to cut; the split between maintenance and growth is not stated. Cash interest paid is lower than interest and debt expense because the first coupon on the notes was paid only on 2026-08-01.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C07

Liquidity adequacy. Cash and revolver availability of USD 531.98 million cover the USD 17.98 million and USD 16.5 million due in the next two fiscal years several times over, and the issuer plans to repay about USD 150 million. The AR securitization facility counts toward liquidity only when the issuer states availability, and at the latest two dates it states no availability; it is secured by U.S. receivables and its lender needed a waiver, so it is treated as working-capital funding rather than committed liquidity.

- High: Issuer-adjusted EBITDA rests on fourteen add-backs for fiscal 2026 that the issuer does not classify as cash or non-cash, recurring or realised, and the Credit Agreement measure adds an annualisation of Kito Crosby, the divestiture and expected synergies that cannot be reproduced. The adjusted ratios are therefore usable as the issuer's view only; component support from the issuer and the credit agreement definitions would close this.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14

- High: Covenant headroom is not established: the credit agreement's first lien leverage ceiling of 7.75x is not matched by a reported first lien ratio, and the waiver of the AR securitization facility's delinquency and default ratios at 2026-09-30 and its amendment on 2026-10-29 are described but not supplied. The test levels, definitions and any cure terms would be needed to size headroom.

- Medium: The acquired business's own statements and pre-acquisition earnings are not supplied, so the twelve-month figures hold Kito Crosby only from 2026-02-03 and no full-year pro forma EBITDA other than the issuer's annualised figure can be built. This understates the earnings base and overstates reported leverage until twelve months of actual results exist.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 14

- Medium: Legal ranking, lien priority and guarantor scope across the term loan, notes, revolver and AR facility are not stated in the documents read, so the debt stack chart has no ranked rows and no secured or senior subtotal is formed. The credit agreement, indenture and guarantee schedules would close this.

- Medium: The annual report prints the revolver maturity as 2028-02-03 in one paragraph and as 2031-02-03 in the next, and the September 2026 report states 2031-02-03. The later date is used; the earlier one may carry over from the previous facility. The credit agreement would settle it.

- Medium: The market risk section of the annual report states there are no pay-fixed swaps while the derivatives note describes eleven with a notional of USD 965 million, so the hedged share of the floating-rate debt is not established. Interest sensitivity to rates therefore cannot be sized.

- Medium: Free cash flow and operating cash flow include deal, integration and refinancing cash costs that the documents do not separate, so underlying cash generation and the run rate after integration are not established. A cash flow bridge from the issuer would close this.

- Low: The annual report's own date is recorded by its signature page as 2026-06-08 while two later quarterly reports say it was filed on 2026-06-02. This changes no figure but the filing date remains unresolved; the filing record would settle it.

- Low: The June 2026 release prints closing cash of 97,234 for fiscal 2026 against 97,023 in the annual report and in its own roll-forward; the annual report figure is used and the difference is 0.211 US$m.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 78

- Low: Issuer-adjusted EBITDA for the first half of fiscal 2027 differs by 0.021 US$m from the two quarters because the six-month stock-based compensation add-back differs; the six-month figure is used.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-07-30_exhibit99107302026.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13

- Low: No release states issuer-adjusted EBITDA for fiscal 2024, the third quarter of fiscal 2026 or the nine months to 2025-12-31, so those cells are not supplied; depreciation and amortization for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 is calculated because no document prints it.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2025-12-31_cmco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7

- Low: Source dashes are carried as not supplied rather than zero, including the fiscal 2025 sale-of-business proceeds and the preferred stock and noncontrolling interest lines at March 2025; the noncontrolling interest and equity attributable lines are not printed in the December 2025 report.

- Low: The company reports one segment, so no segment revenue schedule is built, and capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth; backlog and receivable statistics after March 2026 are not stated in the later releases, and the issuer states no funds-from-operations measure, so none is built.

- Low: Small uncommitted non-U.S. bank lines of USD 5.438 million, of which USD 0.566 million was drawn, and USD 18.757 million of bank guarantees in use are not part of the debt instrument table or total debt, and where the drawn amount is classified is not stated; the amounts are immaterial to leverage but would be debt-like if drawn.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31

- Low: Pension and operating lease balances are taken at March 2026 only and their September 2026 values are not extracted, and the terms of the preferred dividend between cash and payment in kind are stated but the election for the current year is not.

- Low: The issuer's Credit Agreement net debt deducts AR securitization obligations of 42.762 while the September 2026 report prints 42.588, and the earnings bases differ, so the issuer's 4.9x cannot be reconciled to carrying net debt line by line.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Creditors now rest on a larger and more leveraged industrial business whose credit case depends on integrating Kito Crosby, a USD 2,811.91 million all-cash purchase financed by new capital that was 76.12% secured debt and 23.88% CD&R senior preferred.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 86–87; calculation C01; calculation C02

The business sells products that management calls safety-critical through distributors, and Kito Crosby already supplies 56.50% of first-half sales, but the issuer's own leverage measure still adds back USD 132.39 million of annualised earnings and synergies. Sponsor and governance risk is medium: CD&R supplied equity and shows no documented extraction, yet the investment agreement, board terms and proxy statement were not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C07; calculation C10
### Key findings

A material part of the earnings behind the leverage measure is annualised, not yet earned. Kito Crosby supplied 15.76% of FY2026 net sales but 56.50% of H1 FY2027 net sales, and the issuer's Credit Agreement measure adds USD 132.39 million, or 28.30% of its USD 467.80 million twelve-month earnings figure, for a full year of Kito Crosby, the divestiture and expected synergies. That add-back was 59.94% of the measure at March 2026, when it included USD 70.64 million of expected synergies. Creditors should read the 4.9x ratio as management-normalised, not measured.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 15; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C07; calculation C10

The capital structure is debt-heavy with a growing senior equity layer rather than common equity beneath the debt. New secured debt of USD 2,550.00 million and USD 800.00 million of 7% preferred raised USD 538.09 million more than the purchase price, a sum the filings do not break down between refinancing, fees and cash. The preferred accreted USD 37.43 million through September 2026 and the issuer guides to paying it in kind during FY2027; paid in cash it would cost about USD 58.62 million a year on a simple calculation, against USD 4.04 million of common dividends in H1 FY2027. Debt holders gain from the cash retained, but the preferred claim grows ahead of common holders and would compete for cash if the election changed.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 130–131; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C20

CD&R holds influence and a senior claim, but the documents read show no extraction, so governance risk is medium rather than high or low. The investor owns all of the Series A preferred, may name up to three directors, has preemptive rights to keep its pro rata stake and would hold about 43.45% as converted at September 2026 on a calculation that ignores unvested awards, up from 42.48% at issue because the dividend accretes. The annual report itself warns that the investor's interests may differ from other holders. No fees, related-party dealings or creditor-adverse transactions appear in the filings read, but the agreements that would show consent rights and fees were not supplied, so capacity and willingness cannot be separated.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 131; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 159; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C06

The operating franchise is defensive in its consumables and installed base, yet sales are cyclical, distributor-led and exposed to steel and component costs. Management describes the safety-critical products as frequently replaced, most distributors have no written agreement with the issuer, and raw materials were 51% of cost of products sold in FY2026 against 59% a year earlier, a fall that overstates any improvement because the numerator excludes Kito Crosby while the denominator includes it. Hoists are 46.68% of sales, the precision conveying line shrank 3.94% and carries a USD 200.00 million goodwill impairment, and legacy growth is modest: Legacy CMCO net sales grew 5.3% in Q2 FY2027, while total backlog rose 61.12% by March 2026 mainly because Kito Crosby brought USD 199.89 million of it.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 150; 10-Q_2025-12-31_cmco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C23; calculation C24

Capital allocation since closing has favoured deleveraging over distributions, which is supportive but not yet proof. The term loan was cut by USD 191.08 million on the divestiture, USD 7.10 million more than its USD 183.98 million of net proceeds. The issuer plans about USD 150.00 million of repayments in the next twelve months, no shares have been repurchased since FY2025 and the common dividend stayed at USD 0.07 per quarter. Against that, integration and deal costs were USD 65.65 million in FY2026 and USD 30.26 million in H1 FY2027, free cash flow was USD 4.60 million in H1 FY2027 after a negative USD 15.36 million in Q2 FY2027, and capital expenditure is guided up to USD 45 million to USD 55 million. Only USD 14.53 million of the planned paydown is scheduled amortisation, so the rest is an intention, not a maturity.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 111; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 131; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmco-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 51–52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C26; calculation C27; calculation C29

Disclosure supports monitoring, but several items are inconsistent, undated or unexplained, and each caps confidence. The purchase price is printed as USD 2,700.00 million, USD 2,811.91 million and USD 2,821.91 million at announcement, closing and after a final adjustment paid after quarter end. The revolver maturity is printed as 2028 and 2031, and the repayment table supports 2031. The AR facility lender waived its delinquency and default tests at 2026-09-30 and the facility was amended on 2026-10-29 with no reason given. The separation agreement with the officer who signed the annual report as chief financial officer and the successor's offer letter are dated 2026-07-01, which dates a change that the Source readiness analysis could not date, and no reason is stated. Kito Crosby was excluded from the FY2026 internal control assessment while holding 69.72% of consolidated total assets. These are monitoring points, not evidence of conduct.

Basis: 10-Q_2025-12-31_cmco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 111–112; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 155; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C01; calculation C15; calculation C25
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is trading momentum and cash retention. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 20.6% in Q2 FY2027 against 15.4% a year earlier, orders rose 122% largely through the acquisition, and the issuer raised its FY2027 net sales and Adjusted EBITDA guidance twice, to USD 2,130 million to USD 2,170 million and USD 425 million to USD 440 million. Liquidity of USD 531.98 million is far above the USD 17.98 million of principal due in FY2027 and the USD 69.90 million due in FY2029, the sponsor's USD 800.00 million is equity behind the debt and is being paid in kind, and the 50 bp margin cut lowers interest cost. If these hold, the medium governance rating and the doubts about the annualised leverage measure would both ease.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C15; calculation C19; calculation C22

The view would improve if the investment agreement and proxy statement show only customary investor consent rights and no fees, if FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA lands within guidance with synergies realised in cash, and if the planned USD 150.00 million paydown is made while preferred dividends stay in kind. It would worsen if the issuer elects cash preferred dividends, funds further sponsor-linked acquisitions with debt, repeats the AR facility waiver, or lets revolver borrowings reach the 30% level at which the first lien leverage covenant is tested.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C18; calculation C19
### Limitations

- The investment agreement, the proxy statement and the certificates of amendment were not supplied, so the medium sponsor and governance rating could move either way once board composition, investor consent rights, fees and related-party dealings are visible.

- Kito Crosby's own financial statements and pre-deal earnings are not supplied, so the funding finding cannot test the purchase price against acquired earnings; only the earnings figure that management annualises is available.
Basis: 10-Q_2025-12-31_cmco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15
- The purchase price allocation is preliminary and moved in the September quarter, so the asset-quality and goodwill statements in the findings may change before the measurement period ends.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C03

- No guarantor list, collateral schedule or executed debt document is in the set, so the statement that the preferred sits behind all debt rests on the notes' description and the preferred's classification in equity, not on a reading of the legal ranking.
- The two sides of the 2026-02-03 and 2026-03-04 perimeter changes are not like for like, so growth, mix and margin comparisons across them in the findings are directional only.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 57; EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 15

- The reasons for the AR facility waiver, the October 2026 amendment and the change of chief financial officer are not stated, so these are monitoring items and no conclusion about conduct is drawn from them.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

On 2026-02-03 Columbus McKinnon closed its all-cash purchase of all of the equity of Kito Crosby Limited from funds associated with KKR. The price was USD 2,700.00 million at announcement, USD 2,811.91 million at closing including USD 184.31 million of acquired cash, and USD 2,821.91 million after a USD 10.00 million final working capital adjustment that was paid after 2026-09-30. Kito Crosby generated about USD 1,100.00 million of revenue in 2024, and its assets and liabilities are carried at preliminary values with USD 931.87 million of goodwill first recorded. A condition of regulatory approval was the sale of the issuer's U.S. power chain hoist and chain operations to Star Hoist, completed on 2026-03-04 for net proceeds of USD 183.98 million.

Basis: 10-Q_2025-12-31_cmco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 86–89; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C01

New capital was USD 900.00 million of 7.125% senior secured notes due 2033, issued on 2026-01-30, a USD 1,650.00 million term loan due 2033 and USD 800.00 million of Series A preferred shares sold to CD&R, together USD 3,350.00 million or USD 538.09 million more than the price; a USD 500.00 million revolver replaced the old one and USD 75.00 million of it was drawn at closing. The notes pay interest on 1 February and 1 August, are callable from 2029-02-01 at 103.56% falling to 100.00% from 2031, and carry a change of control offer at 101.0%. The term loan priced at SOFR plus 350 bp with a 50 bp floor and was cut to Term SOFR plus 3.00% on 2026-09-21; it amortises at 0.25% a quarter and sweeps excess cash flow at 50%, 25% or 0% depending on first lien leverage. Guarantors and collateral are not named in the documents read.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 110–113; 10-Q_2025-12-31_cmco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; calculation C02

The AR securitization facility, borrowed through Columbus McKinnon FinCo, LLC with the parent as performance guarantor, allows USD 60.00 million at one-month SOFR plus 110 bp to 2028-08-11 and had USD 42.59 million outstanding at 2026-09-30 with no further capacity. Its lender waived the delinquency and default ratios effective 2026-09-30 and the facility was amended again on 2026-10-29. At 2026-09-30 the revolver had USD 59.64 million drawn, USD 19.28 million of letters of credit and USD 421.08 million available, and total debt was USD 2,412.31 million. The only principal due in FY2027 is USD 17.98 million, and USD 2,320.12 million falls after FY2030.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 114–115; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 162–163; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C22

## Findings
### Bottom line
Columbus McKinnon has an adequate business and a stretched financial profile, so creditors depend on Kito Crosby earnings and synergies arriving while liquidity and long maturities buy time.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation N01

Liquidity of USD 531.98 million and no scheduled principal above USD 69.90 million before 2031 support the credit, but quarterly interest cover is 2.31x, free cash flow was only USD 4.60 million in H1 FY2027 and the issuer's 4.9x leverage figure rests on annualised earnings. The main downside is a margin reversal in a distributor-led, steel-exposed business that carries fixed interest charges of USD 185 million to USD 190 million a year.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation N02; calculation N05
### Key findings

Leverage is high, and the lower figure the issuer reports depends on annualised earnings. Net debt of USD 2,301.41 million at 2026-09-30, or USD 2,303.44 million pro forma for the common dividend payable on 2026-11-16, is 6.95x issuer-adjusted twelve-month EBITDA of USD 331.19 million, and 6.95x pro forma. The issuer's 4.9x uses USD 467.80 million of earnings that add USD 132.39 million of annualised acquisition earnings and expected synergies, and reported EBITDA of USD 10.03 million is too small to give a ratio. The twelve-month window holds Kito Crosby only from 2026-02-03, so the ratio falls as acquired earnings enter even if net debt does not, and creditors should underwrite a path down from 6.95x rather than the 4.9x already shown.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 14; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation N01

Cash generation does not yet support deleveraging. Free cash flow was USD 4.60 million in H1 FY2027 after a negative USD 15.36 million in Q2 FY2027, which is 2.07% of H1 Adjusted EBITDA, and negative USD 153.19 million over the twelve months to September 2026 after deal and integration payments. Adjusted EBITDA covered interest and debt expense 2.31x in Q2 FY2027, and the issuer plans about USD 150.00 million of repayments in the next twelve months, of which H1 free cash flow covered only 3.07%. The plan therefore rests on a stronger H2, working capital release or revolver and cash use, not on cash flow already earned.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation N02; calculation N03; calculation N04

Liquidity and maturities are the main support. Cash and revolver availability of USD 531.98 million cover the USD 120.88 million of principal scheduled through FY2030 4.40 times, and 95.05% of principal falls after FY2030, with the revolver due in 2031 and the notes and term loan in 2033. The risks inside that comfort are a revolver draw that rose from USD 12.84 million to USD 59.64 million in the September quarter, an AR facility that has no further capacity and needed a lender waiver, and a 2033 wall of USD 1,449.23 million of term loan and USD 900.00 million of notes that refinancing will test.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–30; calculation N05

The business profile is adequate: replacement-driven products and a wide channel give some stability, but concentration and cost exposure limit it. Hoists are 46.68% of net sales, the United States is 58.14%, there is one reporting segment, and most distributors have no written agreement. Raw materials were 51% of cost of products sold, gross margin fell from 33.8% to 30.1% in FY2026 on tariffs, mix and acquisition accounting, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin of 20.6% in Q2 FY2027 against 15.4% is credited by the issuer partly to the acquired business and synergies. Customer concentration is not stated.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 58; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_exhibit99107302026.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation N11; calculation N12

Financial policy is mixed and governance risk is medium. CD&R's USD 800.00 million of preferred equity reduced the debt needed, the preferred is paid in kind in FY2027 guidance, divestiture cash repaid term debt and no shares have been repurchased since FY2025, yet the purchase was largely debt-funded, the preferred claim accretes ahead of common holders, and the agreements that would show consent rights and fees were not supplied. If paid in cash the preferred would take 27.91% to 32.57% of indicative pre-tax free cash flow from guidance.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation N08

Interest-rate and currency exposure are secondary. Floating-rate debt is 62.87% of gross principal, but the issuer states that 100 bp on the term loan adds only about USD 5.00 million of annual cash interest, which is consistent with about USD 965.00 million of swaps, while the market risk text of the annual report contradicts the derivatives note on whether pay-fixed swaps exist. A 10% move in the dollar changes income from operations by about USD 7.26 million.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 69–70; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 108; calculation N06
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better view is earnings momentum and delivery against guidance. Adjusted EBITDA margin rose 520 bp to 20.6% in Q2 FY2027, Legacy CMCO net sales grew 5.3%, synergies are described as ahead of plan, and guidance for Adjusted EBITDA was raised twice, to USD 425 million to USD 440 million. That guidance needs H2 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 202.35 million to USD 217.35 million against USD 222.65 million in H1 FY2027, so it does not require improvement, and the 50 bp term loan margin cut saves about USD 7.25 million a year. If H2 delivers and net debt starts to fall, leverage on the issuer's own basis would approach the reported 4.9x with real earnings behind it.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation N07; calculation N12

The view would improve if quarterly free cash flow turns clearly positive after integration costs, if the planned paydown is made from cash flow, if the AR facility passes its tests without waivers, and if the missing agreements show customary investor rights. It would worsen if book-to-bill falls below 1.0x, if the Adjusted EBITDA margin slips back toward the 15.2% of FY2026, if revolver borrowings approach the 30% covenant trigger, or if the preferred dividend is paid in cash.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation N08; calculation N09; calculation N12
### Limitations

- No credit rating, market price or peer financials were supplied, so the statement that the business profile is adequate compared with leveraged-credit issuers in the sector rests on the issuer's own disclosures and cannot be calibrated against peers.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The credit agreement and the first lien leverage ratio are not available, so the downside conclusion can show how far the revolver may be drawn before the covenant is tested but not how much covenant headroom exists.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 113; calculation N09

- The twelve-month earnings and cash flow figures are built from unaudited interim reports that hold Kito Crosby from 2026-02-03 only, so the leverage and cash conversion findings move as the window fills with acquired results.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 57

- Guidance, synergy progress and the Credit Agreement measure are management statements, and neither a synergy target nor Kito Crosby's standalone earnings is supplied, so the outlook and contrary-evidence conclusions cannot be tested beyond the arithmetic shown.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation N07

- The annual report contradicts itself on pay-fixed swaps and the notional hedged at later dates is not stated, so the interest-rate conclusion holds only if the derivatives note and the issuer's USD 5.00 million sensitivity are right.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 108; calculation N06
### Company description

Columbus McKinnon designs, makes and markets lifting, rigging, conveying and motion-control products and, since 2026-02-03, includes Kito Crosby, a lifting and securement business that supplied 56.50% of H1 FY2027 net sales. The issuer describes its consumables as safety-critical and frequently replaced, which is management language but points to repeat demand tied to inspection cycles, while hoists, cranes and conveyors depend on industrial capital spending. Sales go mainly through distributors and crane builders, 44% of FY2026 sales were outside the United States, and there is one reporting segment. For creditors the replacement element supports cash-flow visibility and debt service, the cyclical element limits it, and the larger scale after the acquisition helps access to capital markets without removing the integration risk.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation N11
### Ownership and group structure

CD&R XII Keystone Holdings, L.P. holds all of the Series A preferred, about 43% of the equity as converted, may name up to three directors and has preemptive rights, while the common shares are listed and the common holders are not named in the documents supplied. The parent borrows under the 2026 credit agreement and issued the notes, unnamed subsidiaries guarantee the notes, and the AR facility is borrowed through a financing subsidiary with the parent as performance guarantor. Structural priority, guarantor coverage and any unrestricted group cannot be established without the indenture and credit agreement, and the sponsor's willingness to support or extract cannot be inferred from its identity. Sponsor and governance risk is medium on documented behaviour: equity was supplied and no extraction is recorded, but the consent rights, fees and board composition are not visible.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 110; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 130–131; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is partly recurring and partly cyclical. In FY2026 price added USD 21.54 million and volume USD 10.15 million to net sales, and in Q2 FY2027 price added USD 10.06 million against USD 2.34 million from volume, so price supplied 81.14% of the organic gain in the quarter. That points to pricing power, but it also means volume growth is thin, and the issuer ties demand to industrial capacity utilisation, production indices, tariffs and interest rates. Backlog rose 61.12% to USD 519.64 million by March 2026 mainly through Kito Crosby, long-term backlog was 50.8% of the total, and book-to-bill was 1.0x in Q2 FY2027. Sales rest on distributors that choose what to stock and have no written agreements, and no customer or distributor concentration is stated. Revenue is therefore likely more predictable in its consumable and installed-base share, on management's description, and cyclical and discretionary in its project share, and not shown to be concentrated or structurally declining apart from the 3.94% fall in precision conveying.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 150; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation N12; calculation N13
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Costs are weighted to materials and the pass-through is lagged. Raw materials and components were 51% of cost of products sold in FY2026, bought from a limited set of preferred suppliers on company-wide terms, and the issuer reports higher steel and component costs and tariffs. In FY2026 material inflation, tariffs and other cost changes net of price took USD 5.88 million from gross profit, unfavourable mix took USD 7.91 million and the divested business took USD 6.69 million, and the gross margin fell to 30.1% from 33.8% with USD 36.80 million of inventory step-up in cost of sales. In Q2 FY2027 the gross margin was 34.8% against 34.5% and the Adjusted gross margin 36.5% against 35.3%. The split between fixed and variable cost is not stated, so operating leverage cannot be measured; the evidence supports defending margins against input costs with price, with synergy savings as extra cushion, and does not show how margins behave under a volume fall.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 57–58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation N12
### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

Capital needs are light and conversion of EBITDA to cash is weak for now. Capital expenditure was 1.50% of FY2026 net sales and USD 16.46 million in H1 FY2027, with USD 45 million to USD 55 million guided for FY2027, so capex is a lever of some size. Free cash flow was 2.07% of H1 FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA because interest, integration costs of USD 24.30 million year to date, cash taxes and an USD 55.04 million working capital outflow absorbed it, and net cash paid for income taxes was USD 45.85 million in FY2026 despite a net loss. Operating lease payments of USD 23.84 million fall due in FY2027. Deal-related payments depressed FY2026 and the first half, so conversion should improve as they end, but the guidance arithmetic leaves only USD 180.00 million to USD 210.00 million before taxes, integration and working capital, which is the amount that would fund the planned paydown.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 149; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 55–56; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation N03; calculation N08
### Porter's five forces

Competitive rivalry is the force that matters most for margins: the industry is fragmented, rivals include larger groups and some have greater financial resources and less debt, and competition on price could cut margin. Buyer power sits with distributors that decide what to stock and have no written agreements with the issuer, which limits pricing if they favour a rival. Supplier power is moderate: materials are available from several sources but the issuer buys from a limited set of preferred suppliers, and supply constraints have raised cost and lead times. The threat of new entrants and of substitutes is not established in the documents supplied, so no credit conclusion is drawn on either.
### PEST analysis

Two categories change credit capacity. Political and regulatory factors: tariffs raised input costs, and regulatory approval of the acquisition required the sale of the U.S. power chain hoist and chain business, which contributed USD 123.05 million of FY2026 sales and none after 2026-03-04. Economic factors: demand follows industrial capacity utilisation and production, 62.87% of debt floats, and 44% of sales are outside the United States, where a 10% move in the dollar changes income from operations by about USD 7.26 million. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 69; EX-99.1_2026-06-04_exhibit9913312026.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation N06
### SWOT analysis

Strengths are the replacement-driven consumable base, a broad distributor and service network, liquidity of USD 531.98 million with no large maturity before 2031, and sponsor equity of USD 800.00 million. Weaknesses are leverage that is high on actual earnings, thin free cash flow, goodwill and intangibles of 60.30% of total assets, concentration in hoists and in the United States, and cost exposure to steel and tariffs. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are synergy delivery and margin expansion, the 50 bp margin cut, and paydown from a recovering free cash flow. Threats that could weaken it are an industrial downturn with distributor destocking, a cash election on the preferred, a second waiver on the AR facility, and refinancing the USD 2,349.23 million of term loan and notes due in 2033 at higher leverage.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 110–111; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation N05; calculation N14
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength one is liquidity and maturity profile. Cash and revolver availability of USD 531.98 million cover scheduled principal through FY2030 4.40 times, which lowers near-term refinancing and liquidity risk. Strength two is margin and synergy momentum: the Adjusted EBITDA margin rose 520 bp to 20.6% and guidance was raised twice, which would lower leverage if delivered. Strength three is sponsor equity: USD 800.00 million of preferred reduced the debt needed and is paid in kind, preserving cash. Strength four is a replacement-driven franchise whose safety-critical products support repeat demand, with no customer concentration disclosed.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation N05; calculation N12

Weakness one is leverage that depends on annualised earnings: 6.95x on issuer-adjusted EBITDA against the 4.9x the issuer shows, so deleveraging must come from earnings growth and paydown that are not yet in the cash flow. Weakness two is thin free cash flow against fixed interest of USD 185 million to USD 190 million a year, with Q2 FY2027 cover of 2.31x. Weakness three is integration and asset quality: Kito Crosby is 56.50% of H1 sales and goodwill and intangibles are 60.30% of total assets after a USD 200.00 million impairment. Weakness four is cost and demand exposure through steel, tariffs and distributor-led sales. Weakness five is limited visibility of covenant and security terms, with an AR facility waiver and no first lien ratio.
