### Financial profile and credit quality

Business dimensions. Scale and market position is average: pro forma FY2026 net sales of USD 2,035.00 million with leading positions that are management claims and no market share figures. Competitive advantage is average: brands, safety-critical function and a service network support it, but retention, switching cost and pricing power beyond price increases of USD 21.54 million in FY2026 are not evidenced. Business diversification is average: eight product lines and six regions, offset by hoists at 46.68%, the United States at 58.14%, one segment and undisclosed customer concentration.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 150; calculation N11; calculation N13

Operating and cash dimensions. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capex is 1.50% of sales and can be cut, but the fixed cost share is not stated. Margin stability is average: the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.3% in FY2025, 15.2% in FY2026 and 20.8% in H1 FY2027 with tariffs and mix hurting FY2026 and the acquired business and synergies helping since. Free cash flow stability is weak: free cash flow was negative USD 153.19 million over the twelve months to September 2026 and USD 4.60 million in H1 FY2027, and conversion was 2.07% of Adjusted EBITDA.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_cmco-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 61; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_exhibit9911132026.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation N03; calculation N12

Financial dimensions. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: the issuer placed USD 900.00 million of notes and a USD 1,650.00 million term loan in early 2026 and cut the term loan margin by 50 bp in September, but no rating or market price is supplied and leverage is high. Liquidity position is average: USD 531.98 million and a distant maturity profile, against revolver draws that rose and an AR facility without capacity. Financial policy and governance is average with low confidence: equity support, in-kind preferred dividends and divestiture paydown against leveraged acquisition funding and missing agreements. Main supports are liquidity, maturities and margin momentum; constraints are leverage, cash conversion and integration; the trend is improving in margin and worsening in revolver use; missing data are the covenant ratio, rating, Kito Crosby standalone earnings and the investor agreements.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–29; calculation N05; calculation N09; calculation N14
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the issuer guides to FY2027 net sales of USD 2,130 million to USD 2,170 million, Adjusted EBITDA of USD 425 million to USD 440 million and interest expense of USD 185 million to USD 190 million. The guidance is 5.65% above pro forma FY2026 sales at its midpoint and needs H2 Adjusted EBITDA no higher than H1, which supports it, while guided Adjusted EBITDA covers guided interest 2.24x to 2.38x, so deleveraging depends on cash conversion and the planned paydown, not on cover. Company tailwinds are synergy delivery, the margin cut and lower deal costs; company headwinds are interest cost, integration spend and a cash election on the preferred. Sector tailwinds named by the issuer are automation and labour productivity trends and growth in Asia and other emerging markets; sector headwinds are tariffs, steel and component costs and a slowdown in industrial production. Over three to five years the 2029 call date of the notes, the 2031 revolver and the 2033 term loan and notes make deleveraging before 2033 the central task.

### Qualitative downside scenario

The initiating condition is an industrial slowdown with steel and tariff cost pressure that leads distributors, who hold the stocking decision and have no written agreements, to cut orders. The first operational break is a fall in short-cycle orders, with book-to-bill below 1.0x, followed by price giving way to volume and gross margin falling back from the 34.1% Adjusted gross margin of FY2026. Financially, on illustrative arithmetic that returns the Adjusted EBITDA margin to the 15.20% of FY2026 on the guided sales midpoint of USD 2,150 million, Adjusted EBITDA would be USD 326.80 million, interest cover 1.74x, and EBITDA less guided interest and capex USD 89.30 million before taxes, integration and working capital. Cash taxes at the FY2026 level of USD 45.85 million would leave USD 43.45 million, so the planned USD 150.00 million paydown would not be met from cash flow and the revolver would fund the gap. Revolver borrowings could rise by USD 90.36 million, or USD 71.08 million if letters of credit count, before the 30% level at which the first lien leverage covenant is tested, and the ratio against its 7.75x ceiling is not reported. Management levers are capex, which can be cut, the in-kind preferred dividend, a common dividend of USD 8.04 million a year, working capital release from USD 567.55 million of inventory and synergy savings. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis within 12 to 24 months because no principal above USD 69.90 million falls due before 2031, but it is not sufficient to protect the deleveraging plan, and the observable triggers are book-to-bill, the Adjusted EBITDA margin, revolver use, and any new AR facility waiver.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Columbus McKinnon presents an adequate business profile supported by replacement-driven products, a wide channel and added scale, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 6.95x on issuer-adjusted EBITDA (6.95x pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-11-16), thin free cash flow and integration risk. Cash-flow durability appears weak today and not yet demonstrated, because free cash flow was 2.07% of H1 Adjusted EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on cutting leverage before the 2033 term loan and notes come due, on extending the AR facility due 2028-08-11 and on keeping the revolver unused near the 30% covenant level. The primary downside path is a margin reversal on fixed interest charges that forces revolver use and defers deleveraging. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and first lien ratio, the investor agreements, Kito Crosby's standalone earnings, a rating and market prices. Top risk: leverage that depends on annualised earnings and unproven free cash flow.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation N01; calculation N03; calculation N10
